analysis:
The PR adds a single new test file, libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/DarkbloomClusterRuntimeTests/Gemma4TensorParallelTests.swift. It contains Swift Testing cases for the Gemma 4 MoE tensor-parallel plan. The tests check the plan against registered safetensors header fixtures, shard slices against reference slices, two in-process ranks against a split-sum oracle, packed vs separate collectives, and the vocabulary-split head.

Security-relevant behavior examined:
- It only reads fixtures from the repo (StageMetadataChecks/Inputs) and writes synthetic checkpoints to FileManager.temporaryDirectory under a UUID-named directory. Those are removed with defer. There is no production code path, no network or coordinator interaction, no key material, no attestation or authorization logic, and no prompt data.
- Assets A-001, A-003 and A-010 and boundaries TB-002, TB-009 and TB-011 are untouched.
- The synthetic weights are random, so no real consumer data or model weights are exposed. The tests cover CPU only. The optional GEMMA_TP_DIAG path is gated by an environment variable and only prints comparison diagnostics (DIAG lines), with no secrets.
- The tests assert that the plan refuses vision tensors, untied heads, mixed-bit quantization overrides, misaligned configs and out-of-range ranks. These are fail-closed checks that strengthen validation of the shard loader.

Remaining questions:
- The production sources (Gemma4TensorParallelPlan, Gemma4TensorParallelModel, Gemma4TensorParallelLocalPair, Gemma4TensorShard) are not in the supplied evidence. Their security properties are not covered, for example whether the cluster transport authenticates peers or encrypts the all-sum payloads, or whether shard loading validates integrity of the weights (A-004, T-012, T-027).
- Nothing in this test-only change alters the threat model. The test imports use @testable and an SPI import, which is test-only and does not ship.
